description: A front-facing cathedral has two tall pointed side towers flanking a stepped central gable. An arched doorway sits beneath a small cross on the central facade, with both towers rising from a shared flat base.
A church has a tall central gabled nave topped by an attached cross, with lower sloping wings on either side. A rounded doorway opens at the centre of the shared baseline.
A small church has a steep gabled roof with projecting eaves and a cross rising from its apex. Straight walls meet a flat base, where a short central line marks the entrance.
An asymmetric church has a tall cross-topped pointed tower on the left, a lower central gable, and a sloping right annex. Short window marks and a rectangular doorway punctuate the connected facade.
A domed church has one tall rounded central dome behind two smaller side domes. A horizontal band divides the facade above three adjoining arches, with a short window mark in each side dome.

Three domed pavilions rise from a long rectangular wall, with a pointed central dome topped by a cross-like finial. Rounded side domes have small upright finials and horizontal bands, while vertical divisions run down the wall.

Three slender onion-domed towers form a cathedral silhouette, with the tallest tower in the centre. Curved shoulders descend from the central tower toward the lower side towers above a broad flat-bottomed body.
A church has a cross-topped gabled entrance block on the left and a taller pointed tower on the right. A low connector joins them, with a pointed arched doorway and a short tower window.
A church has a cross-topped gabled block on the left and a tall pointed tower on the right. A rectangular middle section connects them, and vertical seams divide the otherwise blank facade.
A church has two unequal pointed towers, each topped by an attached cross, joined by a low rectangular body. The taller right tower and smaller left tower each contain a short vertical window mark.
